excerpt_i18n.en: Over the past six years, domestic GPU companies have been riding the AI wave, with valuations constantly reaching new highs, while DPU has been overlooked. This does not align with industry reality. After NVIDIA completed its acquisition of Mellanox in 2020, it had already established a three-chip strategy of "GPU+CPU+DPU." In recent years, NVIDIA has continued to strengthen its networking capabilities—when Jensen Huang showcased a "six-chip combination" at CES 2026, four of those chips were network-related. An increasingly clear trend is emerging: the bottleneck in AI infrastructure is shifting from computing power itself to networking and orchestration. Especially with the arrival of the era of AI agents, AI systems are shifting from training to high-frequency inference and continuous operation, making GPU utilization increasingly dependent on network efficiency. The DPU has also evolved from a past optional component in data centers to a key role in AI infrastructure. Yet a thought-provoking question remains: since NVIDIA had already bet on DPU, why has the entire industry still underestimated it over the past six years? It wasn't until Yunbao Intelligent's IPO for the first domestic DPU stock was accepted by the Shenzhen Stock Exchange and its prospectus was made public that the market began to realize that a full-featured DPU capable of low-latency, high-bandwidth, and high-performance data scheduling might be the most underestimated piece in the AI infrastructure puzzle. A major chip category underestimated for six years. In recent years, the focus of competition in the AI industry has always been on GPUs—larger model parameters, stronger single-card performance, and more expensive HBM have captured almost the entire industry's attention.
excerpt_i18n.es: En los últimos seis años, las empresas nacionales de GPU han estado en la cresta de la ola de la IA, con valoraciones que no dejan de actualizarse, mientras que las DPU han sido ignoradas. Esto no se ajusta a la realidad del sector. Tras la adquisición de Mellanox por parte de Nvidia en 2020, la compañía ya definió su estrategia de «tres chips: GPU + CPU + DPU». En los últimos años, Nvidia ha seguido fortaleciendo sus capacidades de red, y cuando Jensen Huang presentó la «combinación de seis chips» en el CES de 2026, cuatro de ellos estaban relacionados con la red. Está surgiendo una tendencia cada vez más clara: el cuello de botella de la infraestructura de IA está pasando de la propia potencia de cómputo a la red y la programación. Especialmente con la llegada de la era de los agentes, los sistemas de IA están pasando del entrenamiento a la inferencia de alta frecuencia.

items.title: 物理 AI 到来，移动网络该如何进化？
items.raw_excerpt: 过去一年，几乎所有人都在追问同一个问题： AI 大模型还能变得多聪明？Agent、多模态、端侧部署，构成了 AI 产业最热闹的叙事。 但当 AI 开始进入眼镜、汽车、机器人、摄像头这些物理载体，开始在道路、工厂、家庭和人类交互之后，我们发现，现实世界和 AI 大模型之间，还有最后一公里的路没有打通。 AI 眼镜要识别眼前的文字，Robotaxi 要判断周围路况，机器人要决定下一步动作。它们依赖的不只是算法，也包括图像、语音、位置、空间关系、设备状态和环境变化等数据。 这些数据需要先由终端采集，再通过网络上传，交给云端或边缘侧模型处理。模型输出的结果，也要通过网络返回终端，才能转化现实中的业务动作。 这使得移动网络在 AI 时代承担了新的压力。 过去，网络波动可能只是让视频缓冲几秒；未来，同样的波动可能导致实时识别失败、远程控制迟滞，或者智能体无法完成动作。 移动网络不再只是单纯的内容分发通道。它需要识别连接对象，理解业务类型，判断实时性要求，也要在资源紧张时决定哪些连接需要优先保障。 物理 AI 时代的网络，不能只是一条“更宽的管道”。 移动网络的下一批用户，不只是人类 很长一段时间里，移动通信网络服务的核心对象是人。 在语音时代，网络解决的是通话连接，让人在移动状态下完成实时沟通。进入 3G、4G 时代后，智能手机和在线内容快速普及，移动网络的主要任务转向大带宽数据传输。网页、图片、音乐、视频、直播、游戏和在线会议，成为了移动互联网时代最典型的业务形态。 智能手机也在这个过程中变成了高度集成的入口。过去由独立设备完成的功能，例如 GPS、音乐播放器、相机、录音机和部分办公工具，逐渐被手机吸收到一个终端里。移动互联网时代的一个基本特征，是终端形态向手机集中，人则是最主要的连接主体。 AI 的到来改变了这个前提。 大模型要理解现实世界，首先需要获得更丰富、更连续的现实输入。图

excerpt_i18n.es: Durante el último año, casi todos se han preguntado lo mismo: ¿cuán inteligentes pueden llegar a ser los grandes modelos de IA? excerpt_i18n.en: In the past, reviewing high-light moments from football matches required editors to sift through footage, locate goals, celebrations, slow-motion replays, and audience reactions, then clip, package, add subtitles, and finally distribute to different platforms. The process was lengthy and labor-intensive, and capturing traffic from trending moments depended on human experience and speed. Now this process has been deconstructed and reassembled, with models and toolchains taking over the entire production workflow for match highlight videos. In the new workflow, AI can already understand live streams in real time, identify signals such as camera cuts, audio changes, player celebrations, referee whistles, quickly retrieve highlight clips after key events, and generate independent distributable clips. By the time a moment goes viral, the video is already ready. The underlying change is not just that a specific tool has become more efficient, but that the production method for audio and video content is evolving from human-driven workflows to Agent-driven workflows. This not only involves calling models to generate and process audio and video content but also creates new production tools and workflows based on this foundation, moving closer to the ideal state of "creating a finished video with one command." This paradigm shift in video production requires support from a new technical foundation. Hang Mengyu, Product Manager of the Volcano Engine AI Media Platform, mentioned in a sharing session at the 2026 Summer FORCE Original Power Conference’s Intelligent Video Cloud sub-forum that going from "generating a segment of footage" to "delivering a finished video that can be launched, consumed, and distributed to audiences" still requires a full range of professional audio and video processing work.
